research_approaches.name: Lifestyle-mediated functional improvement
research_approaches.description: Exercise, nutrition, sleep and related behavioural factors that demonstrably improve age-associated function. This is the only category in this list with routine, established human evidence for functional benefit.

uncertainty.description: Functional benefits in humans are well established. What is not established is whether any of it alters underlying aging processes as opposed to improving function at a given age.

research_approaches.name: Senescence-targeting research
research_approaches.description: Approaches that selectively clear senescent cells or suppress their secretory phenotype, studied because senescent burden rises with age and its clearance improved several measures in mice.

uncertainty.description: Animal evidence is the strongest available. Human evidence is limited to small open-label pilots with surrogate endpoints and no control groups.
known_conflicts: Senescent cells contribute to wound healing and tumour suppression, so clearance has potential costs.

research_approaches.name: Autophagy modulation
research_approaches.description: Interventions intended to restore cellular recycling capacity, typically via nutrient-sensing pathways.

uncertainty.description: Autophagic flux cannot be measured in living human tissue, so there is currently no way to confirm target engagement in humans.

research_approaches.name: Nutrient-sensing pathway research
research_approaches.description: Interventions targeting mTOR, AMPK, insulin/IGF-1 and sirtuin signalling, the pathways whose manipulation most reliably extends lifespan in model organisms.

uncertainty.description: Lifespan extension is robust across several species but entirely unreplicated in humans, and the interventions carry meaningful adverse effects.
known_conflicts: Immunosuppressive and metabolic side effects complicate long-term use.

research_approaches.name: Mitochondrial quality-control research
research_approaches.description: Approaches aimed at improving mitochondrial turnover, biogenesis or function.

uncertainty.description: The direction of mitochondrial change differs by tissue, so what counts as improvement is not well defined at the organism level.
known_conflicts: Antioxidant supplementation, predicted to help by the original free-radical theory, has not shown the expected benefits.

research_approaches.name: Regenerative medicine
research_approaches.description: Tissue and organ repair approaches including engineered grafts and cell replacement.

uncertainty.description: Some applications are established clinical care for specific indications; none is established as an intervention on aging itself.

research_approaches.name: Stem-cell research
research_approaches.description: Approaches seeking to restore regenerative capacity by supplementing, replacing or rejuvenating tissue-resident stem cells.

uncertainty.description: Restoring proliferative capacity raises tumour risk that has not been resolved, and delivery to the right niche remains a major obstacle.
known_conflicts: Unregulated clinics market unproven stem-cell products; this category describes research, not available treatment.

research_approaches.name: Gene therapy research
research_approaches.description: Targeted modification of gene expression or sequence, applied to aging-related targets.

uncertainty.description: Delivery, durability, off-target effects and immune response are all unresolved for aging applications, which would require broad rather than tissue-limited delivery.

research_approaches.name: Epigenetic reprogramming
research_approaches.description: Approaches that reset age-associated epigenetic marks, typically via transient expression of reprogramming factors.

uncertainty.description: The central unresolved question is whether regulatory state can be reset without losing cell identity or inducing cancer. Continuous reprogramming killed the animals; only cyclic induction was tolerated.
known_conflicts: Teratoma formation is a demonstrated risk, not a theoretical one.

research_approaches.name: Partial cellular reprogramming
research_approaches.description: Cyclic, incomplete reprogramming intended to recover youthful cellular characteristics while preserving differentiated identity.

uncertainty.description: Demonstrated mainly in a progeroid mouse model, which does not represent normal aging. No human evidence exists.
known_conflicts: The headline result comes from a progeroid model with a short lifespan and an atypical mechanism.

research_approaches.name: Tissue engineering
research_approaches.description: Construction of functional tissue substitutes to replace structures whose function has declined.

uncertainty.description: Structural replacement addresses consequences rather than underlying aging processes, and vascularisation of engineered tissue remains a limiting problem.

research_approaches.name: Immune rejuvenation research
research_approaches.description: Approaches intended to restore thymic output or rebalance an aged immune repertoire.

uncertainty.description: Whether expanding naive T-cell output in an older person improves outcomes, or simply adds cells to a system whose limitation lies elsewhere, is unknown.

research_approaches.name: Microbiome interventions
research_approaches.description: Dietary, probiotic or transplant-based approaches to alter gut microbial ecology.

uncertainty.description: Human microbiome-aging evidence is correlational and heavily confounded by diet and setting. No causal target has been established, so there is nothing yet to intervene on with confidence.
